title.en: 老挝人民民主共和国宪法（2025年修正版）

completenessNote: 自 2026-10-06 全库备份回流（_work/_backup_20261006/data/LA-H046.json）；条文逐字取自该备份，未改写、未补全；原始来源见 source 字段。

text.en:
Each term of the National Assembly lasts five years. 

Members of the National Assembly must be Lao citizens and are elected in accordance with the 

law. 

Elections for a new Assembly must be held no later than sixty days before the current term ends. 

In case of war or other serious obstacles preventing elections, the Assembly may extend its term. 
However, elections must take place no later than six months after conditions return to normal. If 
necessary, the Assembly may hold early elections before its term ends, with the approval of at least 
two-thirds of its members present at the session.

(Amended) 

The Standing Committee of the National Assembly is the permanent body of the Assembly, 

acting on its behalf when the Assembly is not in session. 

12 

 
 
 The Standing Committee consists of a President, a Vice President, and members. 

The President and Vice President of the National Assembly are also the President and Vice 

President of the Standing Committee. 

The President of the Standing Committee, the Presidents of the Commissions, and the Heads of 

the Assembly’s departments may serve no more than two consecutive terms.

(Amended) 

The National Assembly convenes two regular sessions per year. The Standing Committee may 

also convene an extraordinary session if deemed necessary and urgent. 

A session of the National Assembly can only proceed if more than half of its members are 

present.

(Amended) 

A resolution of the National Assembly is valid only if more than half of the attending members 

vote in favor, except in cases stipulated by Articles 55, 67, 69, and 121 of the Constitution.

(Amended) 

A law approved by the National Assembly must be promulgated by the President no later than 30 
days from the date of approval. Within this period, the President has the right to request reconsideration of 
the law by the National Assembly. If the National Assembly confirms its previous decision, the President 
must promulgate the law within 15 days thereafter. 

All promulgated laws must be published in the official gazette, unless the law specifies otherwise.

Issues related to the fate of the nation and the vital interests of the people must be investigated 

and considered by the National Assembly or its Standing Committee.

(Amended) 

The National Assembly shall establish committees and offices to serve as the Secretariat for the 
National Assembly and its Standing Committee, in order to organize and implement their duties within 
the scope of their rights and responsibilities.

(Amended) 

Members of the National Assembly have the right to question the following officials: the 
President, the President of the National Assembly, the Prime Minister, members of the Government, the 
President of the Supreme People’s Court, the President of the Supreme People’s Prosecutor Office, the 
President of the State Inspection Authority, the Head of the Central Anti-Corruption Authority, and the 
President of the State Audit Organization. 

14 

 
 
 
 Persons being questioned must respond before the National Assembly, either verbally or in 

writing.

A member of the National Assembly shall not be subject to criminal proceedings, arrest, 

detention, or imprisonment unless permission is granted by the National Assembly or its Standing 
Committee. 

In cases involving an immediate offense or other urgent circumstances, the relevant authorities 

shall promptly report the matter to the National Assembly or its Standing Committee for deliberation. 

Ongoing investigations must not obstruct the participation of a National Assembly member in 

Assembly meetings. 

Chapter VI 
The President of the State

(Amended) 

The President is the Head of State of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic, and represents the 

multiethnic Lao people both domestically and internationally. The President serves as the Chairman of the 
National Defense and Security Committee, and the Commander-in-Chief of the People’s Armed Forces. 
The President’s role is to guarantee the independence, sovereignty, territorial integrity, stability, and 
security of the nation.

(Amended) 

The President is elected by the National Assembly with a vote of more than two-thirds of its 

attending members. 

The term of office of the President is equal to that of the National Assembly, and one individual 

may serve no more than two consecutive terms. 

The President has an Office of the President to assist in carrying out their duties.

The President has a Vice President, elected by the National Assembly with a vote of more than 

two-thirds of its attending members. 

The Vice President performs duties as assigned by the President and represents the President 

during times when the President is occupied. 

If the President is unable to carry out their responsibilities, the Vice President shall serve as acting 

President until a new President is elected by the National Assembly. 

Chapter VII 

16

The Government 

The Government is the executive branch responsible for state administration in a unified and 

comprehensive manner throughout the country. 

The Government is accountable to the National Assembly and the President of the State.

The Government consists of the Prime Minister, Deputy Prime Ministers, Ministers, and Heads of 

Ministry-equivalent organizations. 

The Government’s term shall be equal to that of the National Assembly. Members of the 

Government may serve for no more than two consecutive terms.

(Amended) 

The Prime Minister is the head of the Government and its representative. They lead and direct the 

Government’s operations and the local administrations. The Prime Minister has the authority to appoint, 
transfer, or remove Vice Ministers, Vice-Chairpersons of ministry-equivalent organizations and heads and 
deputy heads of sub-ministries, Directors-General; and the Heads  of the local commissions of the Capital 
and Provinces, following confirmation by the respective Provincial People’s Assemblies. 

They may also propose the promotion or dismissal of officers with the rank of General or Colonel 

within the national defense and public security forces.

(Amended) 

The Deputy Prime Ministers assist the Prime Minister in leading Government operations and 

local administrations and are responsible for specific portfolios assigned by the Prime Minister. 

In the absence or incapacity of the Prime Minister, one of the Deputy Prime Ministers will serve as acting 
Prime Minister.

Ministers and Heads of ministry-equivalent bodies are responsible for implementing and 
expanding resolutions from the National Assembly, its Standing Committee, and the Government. They 
are to lead, manage, and supervise the execution of work within their sectors and coordinate with others, 
and sign treaties and agreements with foreign countries based on Government approval. 

18

Any member of the Government or the entire Cabinet of Ministers may be subject to a vote of no 

confidence by the National Assembly if the Standing Committee of the National Assembly or at least 
one-fourth of all National Assembly members submit such a motion. 

In the event that a vote of no confidence is passed, the President may propose for the National 

Assembly to reconsider or may decide to dismiss the concerned member(s) of Government. 

Chapter VIII 
Local People’s Assemblies

(Amended) 

The Local People’s Assembly is the representative body of the rights and interests of the Lao 
multi-ethnic people. It is the state authority at the local level, responsible for enacting legally binding 
resolutions within its jurisdiction, deliberating fundamental issues of the locality, and monitoring the work 
of local state bodies. 

Local People’s Assemblies are established according to levels of local governance, including the 

provincial level, the district level, and the sub-district level.The district and sub-district People’s 
Assemblies may be established based on a resolution of the National Assembly. 

The term of the Local People’s Assemblies shall be equal to that of the National Assembly.

(Amended) 

The Standing Committee of the Provincial People’s Assembly is the executive body of the 

Provincial People’s Assembly and acts on its behalf during periods when the assembly is not in session. 

The Standing Committee is composed of a President, Vice President, and members. 

The President and Vice President of the Provincial People’s Assembly concurrently serve as the 

President and Vice President of the Standing Committee. 

The President of the Standing Committee, Chairpersons of committees, and Heads of departments 

within the Provincial People’s Assembly may serve no more than two consecutive terms.

(Amended) 

The Provincial People’s Assembly shall convene two regular sessions per year. The Standing 
Committee of the Provincial People’s Assembly may also convene an extraordinary session if deemed 
necessary and urgent. 

A session may proceed only when more than half of all members of the Provincial People’s 

Assembly are present.

Resolutions of the Provincial People’s Assembly shall be valid only when they receive a majority 

vote from the attending members of the Assembly.

(Amended) 

The Provincial People’s Assembly shall establish various committees and offices to act as 
secretariat for the Assembly and its Standing Committee in the performance of their duties and within the 
scope of their rights.

(Amended) 

Members of the Provincial People’s Assembly have the right to question the following officials: 

the Chairpersons of Capital and Provincial Administrative Committees; Heads of departments and 
department-equivalent bodies at the provincial level; Chairpersons of District and Capital Administrative 
Committees; Presidents of the People’s Courts; Heads of the People’s Prosecutor’s Office at the provincial 
and capital levels; Regional Audit Chairpersons; Provincial Heads of the State Inspection Authority; and 
Heads of provincial-level anti-corruption bodies. 

Those questioned must provide explanations to the Assembly either verbally or in writing.

(Amended) 

A member of the Provincial People’s Assembly shall not be subject to criminal prosecution, 

arrest, detention, or imprisonment unless prior approval is obtained from the Assembly or its Standing 
Committee. 

In cases involving an immediate offense or other urgent circumstances, the relevant authorities 

must immediately report to the Assembly or its Standing Committee for consideration. 

21 

 
 
 Ongoing investigation or interrogation shall not be a reason for preventing the member from 

participating in Assembly sessions. 

CHAPTER IX  
Local Administration

(Amended) 

The Lao People’s Democratic Republic divides local administration into three levels: the 

Provincial level, the District level, and the Sub-district level. 

Villages are recognized as community organizations.

(Amended) 

Local administrative bodies are the administrative organs at the local level. They are responsible 

for comprehensively managing state administration within their jurisdictions. 

Local administrative bodies are accountable to the Government and to their respective local 

people’s assemblies. 

They consist of the Administrative Committees at the Provincial, District, and Sub-district level. 

Each Administrative Committee comprises a Chairperson, Vice Chairperson(s), and members. 

The term of office of each Administrative Committee shall be equal to the term of the 

corresponding local people’s assembly.

(Amended) 

The People’s Courts are judicial authorities. Only People’s Courts have the exclusive right to 

adjudicate and render judgments on cases in the Lao People’s Democratic Republic. 

They operate at three levels: first instance, appellate, and cassation. 

The People’s Courts have the duty to protect justice, individual rights, the democratic people’s 

regime, and the legitimate interests of the state, collectives, and individuals or entities in accordance with 
the law.

(Amended) 

The court system of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic consists of the Supreme People’s 
Court, Local People’s Courts, and Military Courts as stipulated by law. 

Specialized courts may be established as necessary, subject to approval by the Standing 
Committee of the National Assembly.

(Amended) 

The Supreme People’s Court is the highest judicial authority of the Lao People’s Democratic 

Republic. 

It has the power to review, unify court judgments, and supervise the enforcement of final court 

decisions across all levels.

(Amended) 

The President of the Supreme People’s Court is elected or removed by the National Assembly. 

Their term matches the term of the National Assembly, and they may not serve more than two consecutive 
terms. 

23 

 
 
 
 The Vice President of the Supreme People’s Court is appointed, reassigned, or dismissed by the 

President of the State. 

The heads of judicial panels of the Supreme People’s Court and judges of the People’s Courts are 

appointed, reassigned, or dismissed by the Standing Committee of the National Assembly.

(Amended) 

The People’s Courts adjudicate in judicial panels, and decisions are made based on a majority 

vote, except in cases where the law allows for a single judge to decide. 

During deliberations, judges must be independent and adhere strictly to the law.
Court hearings must be public, except in cases otherwise specified by law.

(Amended) 

Litigants have the right to contest and debate in legal proceedings. 

The accused has the right to be informed, to defend against the charges, and to contest the case 

either personally or through legal counsel. 

Lawyers have the right to assist litigants and the accused with legal representation and defense.

(Amended) 

Representatives of social organizations and citizens have the right to participate in court 

proceedings as stipulated by law.

(Amended) 

Final decisions of the People’s Courts must be respected and enforced by all Party and state 

organizations, the Lao Front for National Development, Lao Veterans’ Federation, mass organizations, 
social organizations, international organizations, and all citizens. 

Individuals, legal entities, and relevant organizations must strictly comply.

(Amended) 

The People’s Prosecutor Office is the institution responsible for prosecuting defendants in court 

and overseeing compliance with the law and legal proceedings in the justice system.

The People’s Prosecutor Office of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic consists of the Supreme 
People’s Prosecutor Office, the Local People’s Prosecutor Offices, and the Military Prosecutor Offices as 
defined by law. 

24

(Amended) 

The Head of the Supreme People’s Prosecutor Office leads and supervises the operations of all 

levels of the People’s Prosecutor Office.

(Amended) 

The President of the Supreme People’s Prosecutor Office is elected or removed by the National 

Assembly. Their term is equal to that of the National Assembly, and they may serve no more than two 
consecutive terms. 

The Vice President is appointed, reassigned, or dismissed by the President of the State. 

Other senior officials and staff of the People’s Prosecutor Office, including heads and deputies of 

local and military prosecutor offices, are appointed, reassigned, or dismissed as specified by law.

(Amended) 

During the course of legal proceedings, staff of the People’s Prosecutor Office must act strictly in 

accordance with the law. 

CHAPTER XI  
State Inspection and State Audit

(New) 

State inspection refers to the operations of the State Inspection Authority in monitoring the 
implementation of policies, laws, mandates, rights, duties, and responsibilities of organizations and 
individuals. It also includes proposing solutions and corrective measures in accordance with the law.

(New) 

The State Inspection Authority is responsible for monitoring, inspecting, preventing, and 

combating corruption, as well as reviewing and resolving violations of the law. 

The organizational structure of the State Inspection Authority is defined by law.

(New) 

The Chairperson of the State Inspection Authority is elected or removed by the National 

Assembly and is accountable to the President, the National Assembly, for tasks involving state 
inspections, anti-corruption, and reviewing and resolving violations. 

The Chairperson may serve no more than two consecutive terms. 

The Vice-Chairperson is appointed, transferred, or dismissed by the President. 

25 

 
 
 Chairpersons and Vice-Chairpersons of inspection authorities at each level are appointed, 

reassigned, or removed as defined by law.

(Amended) 

State audit refers to the operations of the State Audit Organization in examining the management 

and use of the state budget, finances, and public assets.

(Amended) 

The State Audit Organization is responsible for auditing and verifying the accuracy of, proposing 

corrective measures to, and following up on implementation of audit findings. 

The organizational structure of the State Audit Organization is defined by law.

(Amended) 

The President of the State Audit Organization is elected or dismissed by the National Assembly 

and is directly accountable to the National Assembly. They must also report to the President, Prime 
Minister, and Standing Committee of the National Assembly regarding the audit work. 

The President may serve no more than two consecutive terms. 

The Vice President is appointed, transferred, or dismissed by the President. 

26

(Amended) 

The State Audit Organization has the following rights and duties: 

1.  To conduct independent audits according to law to verify the correctness of the preparation, 
amendment of the state budget, revenue plans, expenditure plans, investment plans, revenue 
projections, financial reports, legal compliance, and implementation outcomes; 

2.  To manage and monitor its own operations as well as those of regional audit offices as prescribed 

by law; 

3.  To report its activities and audit results as required by law; 

4.  To propose to relevant parties the implementation of necessary measures in response to legal 

violations found in audit results. 

Chapter XII  
Election Committees

(Amended) 

The Election Committee consists of the National Election Committee and the Local Election 

Committees. 

The National Election Committee is established by the Standing Committee of the National 
Assembly and officially proclaimed by the President. It is responsible for overseeing the election of 
members of the National Assembly, members of the Local People’s Assemblies, and the establishment of 
local election committees. 

The Local Election Committees are established and officially proclaimed by the Standing 

Committees of the respective Local People’s Assemblies. They are responsible for implementing the 
plans of the National Election Committee within their jurisdiction for the election of members of the 
National Assembly and members of Local People’s Assemblies.

(Amended) 

Both the National and Local Election Committees are composed of a Chairperson, 

Vice-Chairperson, and members. 

The term of the National Election Committee ends after the first session of the newly elected 

National Assembly. 

The term of Local Election Committees ends after the first session of the newly elected Local 

People’s Assembly at that level. 

The rights and duties of both National and Local Election Committees are defined by law. 

27 

 
 
 Chapter XIII 
Language, Script, National Emblem, National Flag, National 
Anthem, National Day, Currency, and Capital
The Lao language and Lao script are the official language and script of the country.

The national emblem of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic is circular. At the bottom, there is 

an image of half a cogwheel, above which is a red banner inscribed with the words: “Lao People’s 
Democratic Republic.” On both sides are stalks of fully ripe rice, forming a crescent shape. Another red 
banner across the middle bears the words: “Peace, Independence, Democracy, Unity, and Prosperity.” In 
the center of the circle are images of the That Luang stupa, a road, rice fields, forests, and a hydroelectric 
dam.

The national flag of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic has a blue field with red stripes on the 

top and bottom. A white moon is centered in the middle of the blue band. The height of the flag is 
two-thirds its length. Each red stripe is half the height of the blue band. The diameter of the white moon is 
four-fifths the height of the blue band.

The national anthem of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic is the song titled “Pheng Xat Lao” 

(The Lao National Anthem).

The National Day of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic is December 2, 1975, which marks 

the founding of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic.
The currency of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic is the Kip.

The capital city of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic is Vientiane Capital. 

28 

 
 
 
 
 Chapter XIV 
Final Provisions

(Amended) 

The Constitution of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic is the fundamental law of the nation. 

All other laws must conform to the Constitution. 

The state has designated August 15, 1991, as National Constitution Day.

Only the National Assembly has the power to amend the Constitution of the Lao People’s 

Democratic Republic. 

The Constitution shall be adopted only when more than two-thirds of the total number of National 

Assembly members vote in favor.

(Amended) 

This revised Constitution shall take legal effect from the day the President of the Lao People’s 

Democratic Republic issues a presidential decree to promulgate it. 

This Constitution replaces the previous Constitution of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic, 

No. 63/NA, dated 8 December 2015. 

President of the National Assembly 

[Seal and signature of the National Assembly President] 

Dr. Saysomphone Phomvihane 

29
